messages:
kevin: Heads-up — apac-west-1 GPUs started showing 95th+ token latency spikes around 03:20 UTC. Looks like short microbursts from a few tenants are causing PCIe/egress queuing and kvcache churn. Can we decide a short-term isolation approach?

alex: Which pools/racks are impacted? link: https://telemetry.redwood/apac-west/summary?id=apw1-tiles — I see 3 racks with sustained iowait on pcie0.

kevin: Yep racks r03-r05. Spike shapes align with many small low-priority jobs that suddenly ramped. Not a software bug, more like cross-tenant resource bleed.

maya: Confirmed. kvcache miss-rate jumps then we see tail due to DMA bursts. My quick mitigation idea: mark r03/r04 as "islanded" (no backfill from best-effort pools) and route soft-preemptible requests elsewhere for 30m. That avoids a full drain and keeps dedicated customers stable.

samir: Islanded = stop opportunistic backfill, right? That will reduce effective pool capacity in APAC by ~16-20% depending on placement. We should estimate cost of spillover to eu-west and potential latency increase for some tenants.

jess: Alternative: temporarily raise QoS tag for those racks and apply a PCIe-throttle eBPF policer to top offenders. Less capacity hit but more fiddly.

maya: eBPF route is neat but takes ~15m to roll safely (policy + canary). Islanded can be a single config flip. Which do we prefer for 03:30 window?

alex: I'm leaning Islanded for immediate relief. Then follow-up with policer rollout as a medium-term fix. Need approval from SRE on the consumer impact.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-3521 — "APAC apw1 microburst isolation"

kevin: Action plan: 1) Maya toggles islanded on r03/r04, 2) Samir kicks routing to spill to eu-west soft-lane for preemptible requests, 3) Jess starts preparing eBPF policer canary. I'll notify affected tenant owners. Anybody object? :eyes:

samir: FYI capacity calc: moving those backfills will increase eu-west preemptible utilization by ~9% — still under our buffer. Cost delta ~= $1.1k/hr if spill persists. We should set an automated revert after 45m unless spikes persist.

jess: I'll capture the policer policy here for review:
```
# eBPF policer example (draft)
map qdisc_pci = {
  max_bytes: 50MB,
  window_ms: 200,
  penalty_ms: 300
}
# attach to pcie0 transmit queue for tenant flows tagged T=best-effort
```

maya: Toggling islanded now on r03/r04. CLI: `infractl racks set-island r03,r04 --reason "apac microburst 03:20" --ttl 45m`

kevin: Thx. Noting we should add telemetry alert for kvcache miss-rate + pcie-queue depth composite so we can auto-island next time.

ops-bot: INC-3521 updated: islanded applied to r03,r04 by maya at 03:28 UTC

alex: Early signs look good — 95th latency is already back down on requests routed to rest of fleet. Still watching tail on r05.

maya: Will try soft-drain r05 for 10m and then re-evaluate.

samir: Putting a note on cost: if we hit >30m we'll propose an after-action to decide policy (auto-island thresholds vs policer ops).

jess: Can we file a short runbook change: add "islanded" as first-tier mitigation + policer as second? I'll draft.

kevin: Perfect. Closing loop: maya monitor for 60m, if stable we revert islanding after TTL. If spikes recur, escalate to fleet-wide policer rollout. :thumbsup:

maya: Monitoring — will update here.

kevin: Thanks everyone.
